title: Doctor & pharmacy
description: Symptoms, body parts, appointments, the pharmacy and medicine.

distractors: I'm feeling much better.
I'm a bit tired today.
My whole body aches.

items.korean: 너 괜찮아? 얼굴이 안 좋아 보여.
items.english: Are you okay? You don't look well.
items.note: 보여 after an adjective means 'looks/seems': 좋아 보여 = looks good.
distractors: Are you okay? You look tired.
Are you okay? Your face is red.
You look great today.

good.english: I think I caught a cold.

items.note: Doctors ask this to mean 'What's wrong?'. 아프세요 is the honorific of 아파요.
distractors: When did it start hurting?
Does it hurt a lot?
Which hospital are you going to?

items.english: I've had a headache since this morning.
distractors: I've had a stomachache since this morning.
I had a headache yesterday.
My head hurts every morning.

items.english: to come out, to break out (fever, cough)

items.note: 열이 나다 = to run a fever. Without the particle, 열 is also 'ten'.
distractors: I feel cold.
I have a cough.
I'm sweating a lot.

good.english: Since when have you had a fever?

items.english: I've had a fever and a cough since yesterday.
distractors: I've had a fever since this morning.
I had a cough yesterday, but it's gone now.

items.english: I have a runny nose and a sore throat.
distractors: I have a stuffy nose and a headache.
My neck hurts from sleeping badly.
I have a cough and a fever.

good.english: Do you have a fever too?

items.english: I think I've caught a cold.
items.note: 감기에 걸리다 = to catch a cold.
distractors: I think I'm getting better.
I caught a cold last week.
I think it's just an allergy.
I've been throwing up since yesterday.
I had diarrhea yesterday, but I'm fine now.
I've had a stomachache since this morning.

good.english: You need to drink a lot of water.

distractors: I feel sick.
I'm sleepy.
It's difficult.

good.english: Sit down here for a moment.
Since when have you felt dizzy?

bad.english: The room is a bit dirty.

items.english: My stomach hurt, so I couldn't eat.
distractors: I ate too much and now my stomach hurts.
I'm hungry because I skipped a meal.

items.korean: 속이 안 좋고 토할 것 같아요.
items.english: My stomach is upset and I feel like throwing up.
items.note: 속이 안 좋다 = to have an upset stomach (lit. the inside isn't good).
distractors: I ate too much and feel full.
I threw up this morning.
I feel better now, but I'm tired.

good.english: Since when has it been like this?

distractors: My shoulders are stiff.
My legs really hurt.

items.english: I fell and hurt my leg.
distractors: I fell and hurt my arm.
My leg hurts from walking too much.

I broke my ankle.
I sprained my wrist.
My ankle is itchy.

items.english: My eyes are itchy and red.
distractors: My eyes are dry and tired.
My skin is itchy and red.
I can't see well.

items.english: Since when have you been in pain?
distractors: Where does it hurt?
How long will it take?
When did you last eat?
It's been about a month.

items.english: Do you have any other symptoms?
distractors: Do you have any allergies?
Are you taking any other medicine?
Is this your first time here?

bad.english: Yes, we have other colors too.

items.english: Are you allergic to any medication?
distractors: Do you have any food allergies?
Are you taking any medicine?

bad.english: Yes, the pharmacy is over there.

items.english: Are you taking any medicine at the moment?
items.note: 드시다 is the honorific of 먹다; for medicine Koreans say 'eat' (약을 먹다).
distractors: Did you take any medicine this morning?
Would you like to buy some medicine?
Are you allergic to any medicine?

items.english: to open (the mouth), to spread apart

items.note: 보세요 after a verb softens a request: 'try doing'.
distractors: Close your mouth, please.
Open your eyes, please.
Stick out your tongue, please.

items.note: 숨을 쉬다 = to breathe; 크게 (big) makes it a deep breath.
distractors: Hold your breath.
Breathe out slowly.
Get some rest.

items.english: Does it hurt when I press here?
distractors: Does it hurt when you walk?
Where does it hurt the most?
Does it still hurt here?
Let's take an X-ray.
The test results are fine.
Let's do the test next time.

items.english: You need to get an injection.
items.note: 주사를 맞다 = to get a shot (lit. to be hit by an injection).
distractors: You need to take this medicine.
You don't need an injection.
You need to stay in the hospital.

items.english: It's nothing serious, so don't worry.
distractors: It's serious, so you need surgery.

good.english: So I just need to take medicine?

good.english: When would you like to come?

distractors: Is the clinic open this morning?

items.korean: 예약 안 했는데 진료 받을 수 있어요?
items.english: I don't have an appointment. Can I still be seen?
distractors: I have an appointment. Where do I go?
Can I book an appointment for tomorrow?

good.english: Yes, but you'll have to wait a bit.

items.english: Is this your first visit to our clinic?
distractors: When did you last come here?
How did you find our clinic?
Is this your first time in Korea?

Where is the waiting room?

items.note: The residence card foreigners in Korea carry; hospitals ask for it.

items.english: Could I see your alien registration card?
distractors: Could I see your passport?
Could you write down your address?
Do you have a membership card?

items.korean: 여기에 성함하고 생년월일 좀 써 주세요.
items.english: Please write your name and date of birth here.
distractors: Please write your address and phone number here.
Please sign here.

items.english: to call (out), to summon; to sing

distractors: Please come in, the doctor will see you now.

We'll call you when the medicine is ready.

good.english: How long do I have to wait?

distractors: How much is the medicine?

items.english: Here's your prescription. Take it to a pharmacy.
distractors: Here's your receipt. Pay at the front desk.

Bring your prescription next time.

items.english: Take it three times a day.
distractors: Take it twice a day.
Take it three times a week.

good.english: Do I take it after eating?

items.english: Take it thirty minutes after meals.
items.note: 식후 = after meals; 식전 = before meals.
distractors: Take it thirty minutes before meals.

items.korean: 이 약은 먹으면 졸릴 수 있어요.

distractors: This medicine may upset your stomach.
This medicine works quickly.
Take this medicine before you go to sleep.

items.korean: 약 드시는 동안 술은 드시지 마세요.
items.english: Please don't drink alcohol while taking the medicine.
items.note: 드시다 (honorific) covers both eating and drinking.
distractors: Please don't eat anything while taking the medicine.
Take the medicine with a drink.
Don't drive after taking the medicine.

good.english: Do you have a fever as well?

distractors: Do you have any cold medicine?
